narrative:
Homo sapiens, meaning "knowing man," first emerged in Africa [[13]]. The oldest fossils assigned to the species occur in 300,000-year-old rocks from Morocco [[7]], with the species appearing in pockets in the east and north of Africa around this time [[6]]. Other sources date the evolution to approximately 200,000 years ago, with early fossilized remains found near the Omo River in Ethiopia and in what is now Kenya [[4]][[5]]. Homo sapiens evolved from Homo heidelbergensis, which itself evolved around 800,000 years ago and is generally accepted as the ancestor of both sapiens and Neanderthals [[4]][[3]]. The species is distinguished by a cranial capacity of approximately 1,400 cubic centimeters and is notably the only hominid species throughout history to evolve chins [[3]][[8]].

The emergence of Homo sapiens marked what researchers believe was a Cognitive Revolution, the product of new ways of thinking and communicating [[1]]. Between 70,000 and 30,000 years ago, Homo sapiens invented boats, oil lamps, needles, bows, arrows, and art objects [[1]]. By 120,000 years ago, they were heating materials in natural containers [[3]]. Around 100,000 years ago, there were no Homo sapiens anywhere on Earth apart from in Africa, but when they eventually departed the continent and entered Europe and Asia, they did not find virgin territory but land already claimed by other humans [[6]][[2]]. For a time, modern humans lived alongside Neanderthal humans during the Pleistocene [[5]][[11]].

As Homo sapiens entered new continents, they surged across the land as a tidal wave, hunting and killing large mammals until none were left [[2]]. After a few thousand years of human presence, 23 out of 24 animal species on the Australian continent went extinct [[1]]. Other hominid species eventually disappeared as well, and throughout the 11,000 years of the Holocene, Homo sapiens has been the only species of human, one of more than 6,000 species of mammals alive today [[5]][[2]].

The species is characterized as a storytelling animal that thinks in stories rather than numbers or graphs and believes the universe itself works like a story [[9]]. Human morality emerged as a form of cooperation resulting from species-unique forms of social interaction and organization, making Homo sapiens an ultra-cooperative primate [[8]]. When people learned to control nature, it is theorized they invented gods to help them control it more when they failed, and capitalism, a product of the agricultural revolution, developed a relentless pursuit of profit that spurred scientific research [[1]].
